description: A three-input mixer whose sum is folded or wrapped back between a low and a high limit, so a signal that passes either limit comes back inside instead of clipping.

params.text: Adds a fixed voltage to the mix, -10V to +10V, which shifts the sum through the folds with nothing patched.
Sets the low limit the fold works between, -10V to +10V.
Sets the high limit the fold works between, -10V to +10V.
Scales the CV into the low limit, -1 to +1, and inverts it below the centre.
Scales the CV into the high limit, -1 to +1, and inverts it below the centre.
Chooses how the mix comes back when it passes a limit: reflected back and forth, or wrapped round to start again at the other limit. The position it comes up in reflects.
Sets the height of the normalised output, -10V to +10V: positive gives 0V up to that voltage, negative gives a swing of half that voltage either side of zero.

inputs.text: One of the three signals summed into the mix.
Modulates the low limit through the trimmer above it, one volt per volt at the trimmer's full travel.
Modulates the high limit through the trimmer above it, one volt per volt at the trimmer's full travel.
Adds to the normalised output level knob, one volt per volt, the two together held between -10V and +10V.

outputs.text: The folded mix scaled by the normalised output level, rather than by the two limits.
The folded mix, spanning the low limit to the high limit.

notes: The offset knob is a fourth mixer channel with no jack, so the module folds on its own with nothing patched to it.
With the two limits closer together than 0.001V the fold is switched off and the mix output rests at the low limit.
The module is monophonic: only the first channel of a polyphonic cable is read.
The two coloured lamps show the level knob and the normalised output, red for positive and blue for negative.

inputs.5:
±10V · continuous · one channel only

the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±10V.
